learning: When a resolved target is missing, run `ls | grep -i <stem>` in the same bash batch as the existence tests to find the near-match (for example rentl vs rental) for EVIDENCE, so the run does not need a follow-up turn.

Extract with one grep, `(?i)\b(href|src)\s*=\s*("[^"]*"|'[^']*'|[^\s>"']+)` with -o -n, instead of the quoted-only pattern; the quoted-only pattern silently skips uppercase, spaced and unquoted attributes, so a second cross-check grep is not needed.
For a wrong-city finding on a head meta tag, grep that tag across all *.html to see the per-city convention, and compare it with the page's own geo.position before ruling on it.
For wrong-city findings on lead-form payload strings, grep `lead_source_detail` across all *.html in one call. That shows at once whether the tag is a template-wide carry-over or a one-page slip.

When a finding cites a label/href mismatch in a shared footer, grep -o the anchor tags repo-wide, because sibling pages show the correct label in one call, and use -o on long lines because a plain grep returns "[Omitted long matching line]".
